The two triangles shown above are similar. What is the correct similarity statement?
question.worked_solution:
First, let's find the measures of unknown angles. Since the sum of the measures of internal angles of a triangle is ${180}^{∘},$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠K+m∠L+m∠M & ={180}^{∘} \\ m∠K+{90}^{∘}+{53}^{∘} & ={180}^{∘} \\ m∠K+{53}^{∘} & ={90}^{∘} \\ m∠K & ={37}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

Similarly,

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠P+m∠Q+m∠R & ={180}^{∘} \\ {37}^{∘}+{90}^{∘}+m∠R & ={180}^{∘} \\ m∠R+{37}^{∘} & ={90}^{∘} \\ m∠R & ={53}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the triangles are similar, and

$$
\begin{aligned}∠K≅∠P,\,∠L≅∠Q,\,∠M≅∠R.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we conclude that 

- $K$ corresponds to $P,$

- $L$ corresponds to $Q,$

- $M$ corresponds to $R.$

Therefore, $KLM∼PQR.$
